query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding Nb to the CoCrFeNi HEA matrix can overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C.
generation.intervention: Adding Nb to the CoCrFeNi HEA matrix
generation.mechanism: The strong carbide element Nb promotes the dissolution of WC, leading to the formation of NbC, which enhances the solid solution strengthening effect of WC on the CoCrFeNi cladding coating, improving its wear resistance and reducing the coefficient of friction.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance and reduced coefficient of friction throughout the full temperature range
generation.baseline: CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix without Nb addition
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to 800 °C, load: 20 N, environmental conditions: sliding wear test
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of NbC formation and its effect on the wear resistance and coefficient of friction is not fully understood and requires further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test with CoCrFeNi HEA matrix with and without Nb addition, using a pin-disk friction and wear testing machine
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the CoCrFeNi HEA matrix with Nb addition does not show improved wear resistance and reduced coefficient of friction compared to the baseline material, the hypothesis is falsified.

CoCrFeNi HEAs have been widely studied because of their face-centered cubic (FCC) structure and excellent ductility and fracture. However, the mechanical characteristics of CoCrFeNi HEAs are not outstanding [].
It is common practice to add hard WC particles to improve HEAs’ properties [,,,,]. Huang Y et al. [] found that decomposed WC can strengthen the cladding coating of CoCrFeNi with solid solution so as to enhance the hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance of CoCrFeNi HEAs.
The CoCrFeNi/WC HEA cladding coating prepared by LC can only slightly dissolve WC particles, and the distribution of WC particles is uneven [,,]. Hong S et al. [] discovered that the strong carbide element Nb can promote the dissolution of dissolved WC. Wu H et al. [] found that NbC can improve the wear resistance of the coating. ## 2.2. LC Technology
For this experiment, we used the XL-F2000W fiber continuous laser processing system (model: XL-F2000W, manufacturer: Maxphotonics Co. Ltd., Shenzhen, China); the laser output power was 14 kw, a circular Gaussian beam was used, and the spot diameter was 2.5 mm. A multi-track coating was prepared. The wavelength of the laser beam was 1080 nm, the preset powder mode was adopted in the experiment, the laser scanning speed was 500 mm/min, the overlapping rate was 40%, the defocusing amount was +5 mm, and the powder coating thickness was 2 mm using a standard mol

the LC coating. We selected a scanning angle ranging from 20° to 80° according to the actual situation.
Coating cross section hardness test was conducted using Vickers hardness tester (model: MHVD-1000AT, manufacturer: Yizong Precision Instrument Co., LTD. Shanghai, China). Experimental parameters were as follows: load of 200 g and load duration of 10 s. Point spacing was 0.2 mm, and each sample was measured in 3 columns and averaged. The wear resistance of the coated surface was tested using a pin-disk friction and wear testing machine with a displacement sensor (model: SFT-2M; manufacturer: Lanzhou Zhongkehua Technology Development Co., LTD., Lanzhou, China). We used a 6 mm GCr15 steel ball as a counterpart for wear conditions. The test parameters were set to a load of 20 N, a rotating radius of 2 mm, a rotating speed of 200 r/min, and a test duration of 1 h.
